original_question: What is the cosmological origin of the universal thermodynamic arrow of time? In particular, should the present arrow be explained by a special low-entropy condition at the big bang, by a Boltzmann-style giant fluctuation in an eternal universe, or by some other mechanism; and if the low-entropy condition is tied to the big bang, how can one understand the consequences for oscillating-universe models, where the thermodynamic arrow would otherwise have to reverse direction?
target_in_paper: In Section 1 (“Laws and facts”) on page 2, the paper states: “Although irreversible phenomena are mostly observed locally, the thermodynamical arrow of time seems to possess a common global direction. Its origin has, therefore, usually been discussed in a cosmological context. For example, one may assume a special cosmic initial condition at the big bang. Boltzmann, who assumed the universe to be eternal, argued instead that a giant chance fluctuation must have occurred in the distant past in order to form a low entropy state… If, on the other hand, the low entropy is related to a global special condition at high densities, the thermodynamical time arrow would have to change direction in an oscillating universe, while opposite arrows in causally connected parts of the universe seem to be excluded for dynamical reasons.”
correct_elements: The draft correctly identifies: (1) the global thermodynamic arrow of time, (2) the two main proposed cosmological origins—a special low-entropy initial condition at the big bang and a Boltzmann-style giant fluctuation in an eternal universe—and (3) the implication for oscillating-universe models requiring arrow reversal.
missing_details: Explicitly define the thermodynamic arrow of time as a global increase of coarse-grained entropy
Specify that the ‘special low-entropy condition’ refers to a global high-density state at the big bang
Note Boltzmann’s assumption of an eternal universe underlying the giant fluctuation scenario
Clarify what constitutes an oscillating (recollapsing and rebounding) cosmological model
Mention that opposite arrows are dynamically excluded in causally connected regions
refined_question: Given the observed global thermodynamic arrow of time—characterized by a universal increase in coarse-grained entropy—what cosmological mechanism best accounts for its origin: (i) a special low-entropy cosmic initial condition at the big bang (a global high-density state), (ii) a Boltzmann-style giant chance fluctuation in an eternal universe, or (iii) another process? Moreover, if the thermodynamic arrow arises from the big-bang initial condition, what are the implications for recollapsing (oscillating) cosmological models, in which the classical thermodynamic arrow would classically reverse upon recollapse?
justification: This question restates the exact open problem posed in Section 1 of the paper (page 2) by H. D. Zeh, preserving the paper’s scope (global thermodynamic arrow, cosmological origin options, and oscillating-universe arrow reversal) while adding necessary definitions and clarifications to make it self-contained.
